nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

tags.name: param

delta - distance to travel. If delta is \< 0, it will go back,
if it's \> 0, it will go forward by that amount of entries.

the history

during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.description:
History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use

does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.


tags.name: param

nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:

Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.text:

```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use
`createWebHistory` but it requires the server to be properly configured.

does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

tags.name: param
tags.text:
delta - distance to travel. If delta is \< 0, it will go back,
if it's \> 0, it will go forward by that amount of entries.

the history

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: isReady

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async

picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:

during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually

picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:

the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param

nestedMembers.name: isReady

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: isReady

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: isReady

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:

the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: isReady

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: example

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use

does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.name: example
tags.text:

```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

tags.name: param

delta - distance to travel. If delta is \< 0, it will go back,
if it's \> 0, it will go forward by that amount of entries.

the history

nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:

the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.name: isReady

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.description:
History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use
`createWebHistory` but it requires the server to be properly configured.
You can also use a _hash_ based history with `createWebHashHistory` that
does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:

the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

nestedMembers.description: Original options object passed to create the Router

nestedMembers.description: Initial list of routes that should be added to the router.

nestedMembers.name: history
nestedMembers.description:
History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use
`createWebHistory` but it requires the server to be properly configured.
You can also use a _hash_ based history with `createWebHashHistory` that
does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.name: base
nestedMembers.description:
Base path that is prepended to every url. This allows hosting an SPA at a
sub-folder of a domain like `example.com/sub-folder` by having a `base` of
`/sub-folder`

nestedMembers.name: location
nestedMembers.description: Current History location

nestedMembers.name: state

Navigates to a location. In the case of an HTML5 History implementation,
this will call `history.pushState` to effectively change the URL.

data - optional {@link HistoryState} to be associated with the

instead of `history.pushState`

tags.name: param

tags.name: param
tags.text:
data - optional {@link HistoryState} to be associated with the

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

tags.name: param
tags.text:
delta - distance to travel. If delta is \< 0, it will go back,
if it's \> 0, it will go forward by that amount of entries.

tags.name: param
tags.text:
triggerListeners - whether this should trigger listeners attached to
the history

nestedMembers.name: listen
nestedMembers.description:
Attach a listener to the History implementation that is triggered when the
navigation is triggered from outside (like the Browser back and forward
buttons) or when passing `true` to {@link RouterHistory.back } and
{@link RouterHistory.forward }

tags.name: param
tags.text: callback - listener to attach

tags.name: returns
tags.text: a callback to remove the listener

Go back in history if possible by calling `history.back()`. Equivalent to
`router.go(-1)`.

nestedMembers.name: forward
nestedMembers.description:
Go forward in history if possible by calling `history.forward()`.

nestedMembers.name: beforeEach
nestedMembers.description:
Add a navigation guard that executes before any navigation. Returns a
function that removes the registered guard.

tags.name: param
tags.text: guard - navigation guard to add

nestedMembers.name: beforeResolve
nestedMembers.description:
Add a navigation guard that executes before navigation is about to be
resolved. At this state all component have been fetched and other
navigation guards have been successful. Returns a function that removes the
registered guard.

tags.name: param
tags.text: guard - navigation guard to add

tags.name: returns
tags.text: a function that removes the registered guard

tags.name: example

nestedMembers.name: afterEach
nestedMembers.description:
Add a navigation hook that is executed after every navigation. Returns a
function that removes the registered hook.

tags.name: param
tags.text: guard - navigation hook to add

tags.name: returns
tags.text: a function that removes the registered hook

tags.name: example

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

lazy-loaded components have been loaded and were replaced inside the
`components` object) so it can be directly used to display routes. It
cannot contain redirect records either. **This property is non-enumerable**.

nestedMembers.description: Hash of the current location. If present, starts with a `#`.

nestedMembers.description:
Contains the location we were initially trying to access before ending up
on the current location.

passed when adding records. It can also contain redirect records. This
can't be used directly. **This property is non-enumerable**.

nestedMembers.name: force
nestedMembers.description:
Triggers the navigation even if the location is the same as the current one.
Note this will also add a new entry to the history unless `replace: true`
is passed.

nestedMembers.description:

values and some primitives like Symbols are forbidden. More info at
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History/state

members.description: {@link Router} instance used by the application.

nestedMembers.name: options
nestedMembers.description: Original options object passed to create the Router

nestedMembers.name: routes
nestedMembers.description: Initial list of routes that should be added to the router.

nestedMembers.name: history
nestedMembers.description:
History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use
`createWebHistory` but it requires the server to be properly configured.
You can also use a _hash_ based history with `createWebHashHistory` that
does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

tags.name: example

nestedMembers.name: base
nestedMembers.description:
Base path that is prepended to every url. This allows hosting an SPA at a
sub-folder of a domain like `example.com/sub-folder` by having a `base` of
`/sub-folder`

nestedMembers.name: location
nestedMembers.description: Current History location

nestedMembers.name: state
nestedMembers.description: Current History state

nestedMembers.name: push
nestedMembers.description:
Navigates to a location. In the case of an HTML5 History implementation,
this will call `history.pushState` to effectively change the URL.

tags.name: param
tags.text: to - location to push

tags.name: param
tags.text:
data - optional {@link HistoryState} to be associated with the
navigation entry

nestedMembers.name: replace
nestedMembers.description:
Same as {@link RouterHistory.push} but performs a `history.replaceState`
instead of `history.pushState`

tags.name: param
tags.text: to - location to set

tags.name: param
tags.text:
data - optional {@link HistoryState} to be associated with the
navigation entry

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

tags.name: param
tags.text:
delta - distance to travel. If delta is \< 0, it will go back,
if it's \> 0, it will go forward by that amount of entries.

tags.name: param
tags.text:
triggerListeners - whether this should trigger listeners attached to
the history

nestedMembers.name: listen
nestedMembers.description:
Attach a listener to the History implementation that is triggered when the
navigation is triggered from outside (like the Browser back and forward
buttons) or when passing `true` to {@link RouterHistory.back } and
{@link RouterHistory.forward }

tags.name: param
tags.text: callback - listener to attach

tags.name: returns
tags.text: a callback to remove the listener

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial

push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: isEffectivelyChecked
nestedMembers.description:
Determines whether the current tree node is effectively checked.

Rules:
1. A disabled leaf node is always considered checked.
2. A non-disabled leaf node reflects its actual checked state.
3. A non-leaf node is considered checked only when:
   - All of its child nodes are effectively checked, and
   - Each child follows the same evaluation rules:
     - Disabled leaf nodes follow rule #1.
     - Non-leaf child nodes are recursively evaluated under this rule (#3).

members.name: isEffectivelyChecked
members.description:
Determines whether the current tree node is effectively checked.

Rules:
1. A disabled leaf node is always considered checked.
2. A non-disabled leaf node reflects its actual checked state.
3. A non-leaf node is considered checked only when:
   - All of its child nodes are effectively checked, and
   - Each child follows the same evaluation rules:
     - Disabled leaf nodes follow rule #1.
     - Non-leaf child nodes are recursively evaluated under this rule (#3).

nestedMembers.name: history
nestedMembers.description:
History implementation used by the router. Most web applications should use
`createWebHistory` but it requires the server to be properly configured.
You can also use a _hash_ based history with `createWebHashHistory` that
does not require any configuration on the server but isn't handled at all
by search engines and does poorly on SEO.

nestedMembers.name: go
nestedMembers.description: Traverses history in a given direction.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```js
myHistory.go(-1) // equivalent to window.history.back()
myHistory.go(1) // equivalent to window.history.forward()
```

tags.name: param
tags.text:
delta - distance to travel. If delta is \< 0, it will go back,
if it's \> 0, it will go forward by that amount of entries.

tags.name: param

triggerListeners - whether this should trigger listeners attached to
the history

nestedMembers.name: onError
nestedMembers.description:
Adds an error handler that is called every time a non caught error happens
during navigation. This includes errors thrown synchronously and
asynchronously, errors returned or passed to `next` in any navigation
guard, and errors occurred when trying to resolve an async component that
is required to render a route.

tags.name: param
tags.text: handler - error handler to register

nestedMembers.name: isReady
nestedMembers.description:
Returns a Promise that resolves when the router has completed the initial
navigation, which means it has resolved all async enter hooks and async
components that are associated with the initial route. If the initial
navigation already happened, the promise resolves immediately.

This is useful in server-side rendering to ensure consistent output on both
the server and the client. Note that on server side, you need to manually
push the initial location while on client side, the router automatically
picks it up from the URL.

nestedMembers.name: install
nestedMembers.description:
Called automatically by `app.use(router)`. Should not be called manually by
the user. This will trigger the initial navigation when on client side.

tags.name: param
tags.text: app - Application that uses the router

The **`append()`** method of the Headers interface appends a new value onto an existing header inside a Headers object, or adds the header if it does not already exist.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/append)

nestedMembers.name: delete
nestedMembers.description:
The **`delete()`** method of the Headers interface deletes a header from the current Headers object.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/delete)

nestedMembers.name: get
nestedMembers.description:
The **`get()`** method of the Headers interface returns a byte string of all the values of a header within a Headers object with a given name. If the requested header doesn't exist in the Headers object, it returns null.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get)

nestedMembers.name: getSetCookie
nestedMembers.description:
The **`getSetCookie()`** method of the Headers interface returns an array containing the values of all Set-Cookie headers associated with a response. This allows Headers objects to handle having multiple Set-Cookie headers, which wasn't possible prior to its implementation.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/getSetCookie)

nestedMembers.name: has
nestedMembers.description:
The **`has()`** method of the Headers interface returns a boolean stating whether a Headers object contains a certain header.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has)

nestedMembers.name: set
nestedMembers.description:
The **`set()`** method of the Headers interface sets a new value for an existing header inside a Headers object, or adds the header if it does not already exist.

[MDN Reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/set)
